newsitem.title: USA: Central Hudson proposes transition period.
newsitem.headline: Central Hudson proposes transition period.

text.p: Central Hudson Gas & Electric Corp said it has proposed a three year transition to competition in a filing with state regulators.

The filing was made in response to a Public Service Commission order in May requiring electric utilities "to submit their thoughts and ideas on how a transition can be made from a highly regulated industry to one win which regulation is replaced by competitive markets," the company said in a statement.
However, that statement did not address restructuring issues cited by other utilities responding to the order.
Central Hudson spokesman said the filing calls for retention of the company's present, vertically integrated structure.
Five New York utilities are filing in response to the May order which excluded Niagara Mohawk Power Corp and Long Island Lighting Co.
GPU Inc spokesman Gary D. Plummer said the company's Pennsylvania Electric Co subsidiary was told its New York operations were "too small" to require a response to the order.

New York State Electric & Gas Corp filed its proposals Friday, and Tuesday filings have already been announced by Rochester Gas & Electric Corp and Orange & Rockland Utilities Inc, leaving only Consolidated Edison Co of New York Inc unheard from.

"Central Hudson's electric prices are 27 percent below the New York State average and we have had the lowest average price of electricity among the state's electric companies for four consecutive years," the utility pointed out, adding they are also "the lowest in the Northeast."

Citing Edison Electric Institute data for the last half of 1995, the company said its average rate of $0.0861 per kilowatt hour compared to state averages of $0.0939 to $0.1170 for other states in the Northeast.
Citing state data, Central Hudson said its rates compare to $0.0934 to $0.1537 for other areas of New York state.
Central Hudson also noted it has not increased the price of electricity over the past three years despite a loss in sales resulting from the downsizing of International Business Machines Corp.

The utility said it proposes to maintain stable prices for another three years while exploring opportunities to offer discounts to its largest industrial and commercial customers in condideration for their commitment to maintain their businesses in the area.

The company said it proposes to continue providing all the services it now provides during the transition period beginning in 1997 and continuing through 1999 while exploring a pilot program allowing choice of power providers.
Central Hudson said proposes to develop a Customer Service Performance Guarantee Program that would match service quality to customers' expectations.
